entities.summary: Jon Ingesson Kuvlung was a pretender to the Royal Crown during the civil war era in Norway. He was a rival of the reigning King Sverre of Norway. Kuvlung's claim to the throne was largely based on his descent from the ancient Swedish royal house of Sverker. In 1177, he was appointed as the Duke of Norway by the Norwegian nobles, who were dissatisfied with King Sverre's rule. Kuvlung's short-lived reign was marked by power struggles with Sverre, who eventually defeated and imprisoned him in 1180. Kuvlung's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his rival and successor, King Sverre, who went on to unite Norway under a single ruler for the first time in centuries. Despite this, Kuvlung's rebellion marked an important moment in the development of Norwegian identity and the struggle for power in the country's early medieval period. The conflict between Kuvlung and Sverre also had significant consequences for the Viking Age's end and the rise of the Norwegian monarchy in the 13th century. Kuvlung's story highlights the complexities and nuances of medieval politics, where the lines between legitimacy and illegitimacy were often blurred. His ultimate failure serves as a reminder of the brutal nature of medieval power struggles, where the rule of law was often secondary to the rule of force.
